page: Amazon Web Services i8g.16xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 64 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 15,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 38 Gbps, managed via the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core capabilities and top-tier memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier status in memory bandwidth for both cached small blocks and uncached large blocks, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score. Multi-core processing is strong, as evidenced by top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core, software compilation, and PassMark CPU physics tests. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and PassMark CPU encryption tests falling into the average category.

This hardware profile is optimized for data-intensive workloads. It demonstrates top-tier performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput. Large language model inference speeds vary, showing top-tier text generation for medium models and strong text generation for large models, but weak text generation for small models. The combination of high-capacity local NVMe storage, high memory bandwidth, and dedicated arm64 cores makes this instance suitable for large-scale databases, caching layers, and high-throughput web serving, while single-threaded tasks represent a relative performance tradeoff.
